title: Physical and chemical weathering
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:51Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Physical and chemical weathering
card: Weathering is the breaking down of rock where it sits. The rock is not carried away while it is being weathered.

cracks or breaks rock into smaller pieces without changing what the rock is made of. Water freezes in a crack, expands and pushes the crack wider. Heating by day and cooling at night can also crack rock.
changes the minerals in rock, so the rock becomes a different substance or dissolves. Iron in rock can rust. Rainwater can slowly dissolve some rocks, such as limestone.
Both kinds often work together. Cracks from physical weathering let water in, which gives chemical weathering more rock to attack.
draft.remember: Physical weathering breaks rock apart. Chemical weathering changes the rock itself.

opts: Ice widening a crack in a boulder
A rock splitting after hot days and cold nights
A large slab breaking into smaller blocks
a.why: Dissolving changes the rock into a different form, so it is chemical weathering. Ice widening a crack is tempting, but it only breaks the rock and does not change what it is made of.
a.clue: Look for the option where the rock itself is changed, not just broken.

b.q: Red rocks in a dry part of Western Australia turn crumbly and rust-coloured on the surface, because iron in them reacts with air and moisture. What type of weathering is this?
opts: Chemical, because the iron in the rock has changed
Physical, because the rock has become crumbly
Physical, because the rock sits in a dry area
Chemical, because the rock has been carried away
b.why: Rusting changes the iron in the rock into a new substance, so it is chemical weathering. Crumbling is tempting, but the cause is a change in the minerals, not just cracking. Carrying rock away is not weathering at all.
b.clue: Ask what happened to the iron: was it split or changed?

b.best: Chemical, because the iron in the rock has changed
